messages:
maria: Heads-up — onboarding raven-3b hit two issues in staging: weird emoji splitting in outputs and a load OOM when trying the 2-bit quantized weights. weights at s3://redwood-models/raven/3b/v1.2/
alex: Can you paste an example of the emoji split? and which tokenizer file you used?
maria: example: input '\uD83D\uDE0A hello' -> model emits '\uD83D' '�' '�' 'hello' (gets broken). Tokenizer in use is tokenizer.json from the weights bundle.
jin: emoji/unicode splits usually mean a vocab mismatch or wrong normalizer. Did we accidentally use the byte-level BPE vs the new unicode-normalizer pipeline?
maria: I ran a quick diff: tokenizer.json vocab_size = 50258 but model config.json has n_vocab = 50257. Off-by-one. Found via: ```jq '.vocab_size' s3://.../tokenizer.json``` (used local cp). Also saw warning during load: "vocab_size mismatch" in the logs.
infra-bot: [INF-2345] New ticket created for raven-3b tokenizer mismatch: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2345
alex: That explains tokenization. The split emoji is a symptom when tokenizer indices map differently. We should not load that tokenizer in prod until fixed. Is the bundle published to the model-catalog? If so, rollback.
maria: It was pushed to staging catalog only. I attempted a rolling load on a dedicated GPU and hit OOM when loading quantized .safetensors. OOM trace: "CUDA out of memory while allocating KV cache" during init. That wasn't happening with 8-bit. Command I ran: ```python serve_model.py --model-dir /tmp/raven-3b --quant 2bit``` and then GPU memory peaked then crashed.
jin: Possible causes: incorrect state_dict shapes due to tokenizer/model mismatch or a corrupted quant file that expands during dequant. Can you md5 the file and confirm size? Also check loader logs for unexpected layer shapes.
tara: I'm on call for infra, can look in ~10m. @maria can you upload the exact loader logs and the output of `s3 ls --human` for the bundle path? Also ping @alex if rollback needed.
maria: Uploaded logs to the ticket, and `aws s3 ls s3://redwood-models/raven/3b/v1.2/ --human` shows quant_2b.safetensors 3.2G, model.safetensors 12.1G, tokenizer.json 2.1M
alex: 2-bit file size looks plausible. md5sums: I see mismatch with the caller's checksum from the build job — suggests upload might have been truncated earlier. If truncated, loader might misread shapes and try to allocate giant tensors.
jin: Quick triage steps I suggest: 1) pin model->tokenizer mapping in staging to use prior tokenizer that matches n_vocab, 2) re-upload quant file from CI artifacts and verify checksums, 3) retry load with --debug-shapes to log expected vs found shapes.
maria: Doing step 1 now: updated staging catalog to point to tokenizer v1.1 (matching n_vocab 50257). Will run a canary load.
deploy-bot: Canary deployment started for raven-3b -> staging-canary-3 at 1767801500 :rocket:
maria: Canary with old tokenizer loads fine, no emoji splitting in a quick smoke test. Memory usage stable.
tara: I'll take ownership of INF-2345 for the upload/CI checksum fix. @alex can you open a small PR to add a pre-publish checksum validation to the model-publisher? That should prevent truncated uploads.
alex: On it, will draft PR and link to ticket. Thanks for the quick triage team :thumbsup:
maria: Thanks — marking this thread resolved for now, will keep ticket updated.
